skill_context_used.name: physmath-research-loop
skill_context_used.applied_policy: One independent review pass; grounded scientific/numerical findings only; immutable inputs exact, output interpretation scoped; no adversarial multi-user assumptions; no native campaign repetition.

checks.evidence: ObservedDOP853 calls super()._estimate_error_norm once and returns the same actual object unchanged. Diagnostic dots and norms do not write K, scale, or the solver state. Full on/off fixture RHS byte logs, accepted coordinates, endpoint, old observations, ledger and provider errors match exactly.

checks.area: RK stages, dense output and RHS
checks.evidence: Generated base is the actual B1 78386db7... solver; diagnostics-disabled source hash is unchanged. AST of rhs, send, binary IO and norm functions is identical. _step_impl, _dense_output_impl, _estimate_error, step and dense_output resolve to the same installed SciPy function objects.

Each solve invocation records event/retry and retained/discarded state. A failed interval may contain local error-accepted estimates, but final_trajectory_accepted_estimates is zero. Fixture has one discarded attempt containing such estimates, and retained estimate totals equal solver step totals.

Existing physical pre-birth P output is retained before assigning the new birth coordinates; a separate P query occurs after the one original birth assignment. Neither the established observations schedule nor the original RHS calls are changed. Native P accepts immutable Setup and coordinate slices and constructs physical output locally. Nonbirth/gas/ledger bit comparisons are descriptive fields.

Coverage enumerates expected source_inventory births, requires exactly one AVAILABLE record with matching active counts, inventory and birth clock, and marks missing/duplicates/invalid/unexpected records incomplete. Fraction.from_float computes delta N + delta photo events - injected N from exact stored binary64 values, including minimum subnormal fixture. No automatic accuracy certificate is issued.

age32 changes only name and birth_panels relative to age64. Shared q0, n_mu8, source_subdivisions8, transport16, common_birth_levels8/16/32/64, time_factor1 remain. DEFAULT_CASES remains age64,time8,time16,time32,spectral128; the new diagnostic age32 case requires explicit selection.

Before computing metrics, validates COMPLETE status, stored output hashes, q0 reference axis settings, original native SHA, exact computational base solver SHA, same binary/interpreter/numpy/scipy/thread/rpc identity, and equality of non-age config fields. Diagnostic-copy identity is produced only by the exact-base transform. Comparison scope is explicitly finite age32-to-age64 only, with no continuum or production admission.

reuse_compact requires exit0 build, all prepared source output hashes, exact original PREPARED_IDENTITY bytes bound by BUILD_RECEIPT, and exact compact binary SHA. It copies the bound binary/build receipt only after those checks. A mismatched reconstruction cannot be reused; fallback recompilation carries a comparison record and is subject to later same-binary binding.

run.scope: stdlib unit test runner; deterministic fixture native replacement; no native physics campaign

decision: The reviewed S changes are ready for the already-authorized tiny native age2 diagnostics-on/off control. No repair requested by this C9 pass.
limits: This review executed deterministic fixture tests and read native source; it did not execute the native age2 control or any NCP/full native/age64 campaign.
Identical RK/RHS logic and fixture trajectory do not by themselves establish native age32-to-age64 accuracy. The matched-source finite-neighbor comparison remains a future execution result.
The diagnostic old RMS value is descriptive and does not establish RMS dilution as the causal mechanism of prior failures.
Exact jump residuals are exact arithmetic on stored binary64 terms, without a simulation roundoff or continuum accuracy certificate.
